hypotheses.text: Parkinsonism and hypokinesia in ACBD6-related neurodevelopmental disorder represent age-dependent manifestations occurring in only a minority (~32%) of patients, such that progressive early-onset dystonia and postural deformities (present in >90%), rather than parkinsonism, constitute the primary discriminating movement disorder phenotype.
hypotheses.rationale: Resolves the conflict where prior formulations overemphasized parkinsonism as an obligatory discriminating sign. In the largest reported cohort, parkinsonism/hypokinesia was detected in only 32% (14/45) and developed with advancing age, whereas dystonia (94%) and progressive postural deformities (97%) were near-universal, showing that the absence of parkinsonism cannot exclude ACBD6 deficiency in children or adolescents.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 45 individuals with biallelic ACBD6 variants, dystonia was observed in 94% (42/45) and progressive postural deformities in 97% (41/42 assessable), whereas parkinsonism/hypokinesia developed with advancing age in only 32% (14/44 assessable).

source.title: Bi-allelic ACBD6 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with progressive and complex movement disorders
source.quote: The most conspicuous and common movement disorder was dystonia (94%), frequently leading to early-onset progressive postural deformities (97%), limb dystonia (55%) and cervical dystonia (31%). A jerky tremor in the upper limbs (63%), a mild head tremor (59%), parkinsonism/hypokinesia developing with advancing age (32%) and simple motor and vocal tics were among other frequent movement disorders.

evidence.text: Literature review identifies axial dystonia as a key hallmark suggesting recessive ACBD6 mutations in children presenting with hyperkinetic movement disorders and neurodevelopmental delay.

hypotheses.text: Severe visceral and metabolic complications reported in ACBD6 deficiency (cirrhosis, diabetes mellitus, pancytopenia, and end-stage renal failure) represent late-adulthood complications of severe metabolic dysregulation or specific truncating alleles rather than paroxysmal acute metabolic decompensations like organic acidurias.
hypotheses.rationale: Resolves the tension between claims that ACBD6 deficiency lacks metabolic/systemic involvement and Yeetong et al.'s findings of multi-organ failure. The systemic manifestations in Yeetong et al. led to death in the patients' 30s rather than childhood episodic metabolic decompensations (e.g., hyperammonemia, lactic acidosis), clarifying that systemic organ failure occurs late in disease progression.

evidence.text: Two Thai siblings with homozygous ACBD6 c.360dup (p.Leu121Thrfs*27) developed morbid obesity, pancytopenia, diabetes mellitus, cirrhosis, and renal failure, resulting in death in their early 30s.

source.title: Neurodevelopmental Disorder, Obesity, Pancytopenia, Diabetes Mellitus, Cirrhosis, and Renal Failure Caused by Biallelic Loss-of-Function ACBD6 Variants
source.quote: Clinical manifestations that have never been previously reported include morbid obesity, pancytopenia with severe infections, diabetes mellitus, cirrhosis, and renal failure, leading to deaths in their early 30s.

evidence.text: In a 45-patient worldwide cohort, overweight was common (59%) but acute metabolic crises or early primary hepatic/renal failure were not characteristic presenting features.

hypotheses.text: Specific midline structural neuroimaging features (corpus callosum hypoplasia/dysgenesis in ~70% and anterior commissure hypoplasia/agenesis in ~66%) combined with progressive dystonia provide a more reliable phenotypic differentiator for ACBD6 deficiency from NBIA, GNAO1, and NKX2-1 disorders than movement disorder phenomenology alone.
hypotheses.rationale: Movement disorders overlap significantly across childhood-onset chorea and dystonia conditions (GNAO1, NKX2-1, classic NBIA). However, GNAO1 and NKX2-1 typically lack the high rates of anterior commissure and corpus callosum commissural hypoplasia seen in ACBD6, while classic NBIA displays basal ganglia iron accumulation that is absent in ACBD6 deficiency.

evidence.text: Biallelic ACBD6 pathogenic variants produce characteristic midline commissural and brainstem anomalies on MRI, including corpus callosum abnormalities in 70% and hypoplasia or agenesis of the anterior commissure in 66%.

source.quote: Midline brain malformations including corpus callosum abnormalities (70%), hypoplasia/agenesis of the anterior commissure (66%), short midbrain and small inferior cerebellar vermis (38% each) as well as hypertrophy of the clava (24%) were common neuroimaging findings.

evidence.text: Novel monogenic chorea conditions, including ACBD6, present on the background of complex neurodevelopmental phenotypes and structural cerebral changes.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of adult ACBD6-deficient individuals develop multi-system involvement (cirrhosis, diabetes, nephropathy, or pancytopenia) versus purely neurologic phenotypes?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifies whether the severe extraneural features described by Yeetong et al. are typical late-stage sequelae in long-surviving adults with biallelic ACBD6 mutations or an atypical isolate.

new_directions.question_text: Does levodopa responsiveness differentiate ACBD6-associated parkinsonism from other childhood-onset dystonia-parkinsonism disorders?
new_directions.rationale: Evaluating pharmacological response in the 32% of patients with parkinsonism would provide clinicians with both diagnostic differentiation and direct therapeutic guidance.
